Rule_Description: Inference resource sizing must record the model parameter count when the model is parameterized by a known parameter count.
Condition: Parameter count is known for the serving model
Output_Decision: Parameter count is available as an input to inference resource estimation
Evidence: The catalogue provides GPU memory and compute fields, while parameter count is a workload/model input rather than a hardware field.
Applicability: LLM/parameterized model sizing; not applicable where parameter count is unavailable or not meaningful.
Limitations: Parameter count alone does not determine total inference memory because KV cache, activations and runtime overhead vary.

Rule_Description: The model weight footprint must be characterized at the selected serving precision before GPU memory capacity is assessed.
Inputs: Parameter count; weight precision/bytes per parameter
Condition: Model is loaded with a specified weight representation
Output_Decision: Use model weight footprint as one component of inference GPU memory requirement
Evidence: Lower-precision representations reduce model memory footprint; exact footprint depends on representation and quantization scheme.
Applicability: Models whose weights use the stated precision/quantization.
Limitations: Quantization metadata, scales, packing and non-quantized modules can add overhead; do not infer total GPU memory from weight size alone.
Validation: B — formula is derived engineering accounting

Rule_Description: Serving precision must be recorded because precision changes model memory footprint and can change compute behavior on supported hardware.
Inputs: Serving precision; model; candidate GPU precision support
Condition: Serving precision is selected
Threshold_Value: FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 / INT8 / INT4 where supported
Output_Decision: Use precision-specific model and benchmark evidence for resource sizing
Evidence: TensorRT-LLM documents lower-precision formats including INT8, FP8 and FP4; Hugging Face documents FP32, FP16/BF16 and integer quantization.
Limitations: INT4 is not a universal compute mode; some implementations use weight-only quantization with dequantization.
Validation: A — source-supported requirement; hardware support must be validated

Rule_Description: Inference sizing must record intended batch size or batching policy because batching changes throughput, latency and memory demand.
Condition: Batching is enabled or a fixed batch is used
Output_Decision: Use specified batch configuration when evaluating candidate performance and memory
Exact_Source_Title: Dynamic Batching & Concurrent Model Execution — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
Evidence: NVIDIA documents that dynamic batching combines requests and affects throughput/latency; continuous batching forms batches at iteration steps.
Limitations: No universal optimal batch size; latency budgets can constrain batch size.

Rule_Description: Online inference resource sizing must record target request arrival rate when the workload is rate-driven.
Condition: Workload is specified by requests per second
Output_Decision: Use request rate as the load target for capacity/performance evaluation
Hardware_Field: Benchmark throughput; no direct request-rate hardware field
Exact_Source_Title: Performance Analyzer — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
Evidence: Perf Analyzer supports request-rate load mode and defines it as sending N requests per second.
Limitations: Request rate is workload demand, not a GPU capability field; candidate throughput must be measured under comparable conditions.

Rule_Name: Inference Sequence And Context Length Required
Rule_Description: For sequence-generating or sequence-processing inference, input sequence length and maximum context length must be recorded because memory and performance depend on token length.
Inputs: Input sequence length; context length; output length where applicable
Condition: Model uses sequence/context-dependent inference
Output_Decision: Use sequence/context lengths in memory and benchmark configuration
Evidence: TensorRT-LLM documents KV-cache sizing dependence on batch size and max context plus new tokens; GenAI-Perf reports input/output sequence lengths.
Applicability: Autoregressive/sequence inference; exact behavior varies by architecture.
Limitations: Not every model uses KV cache; sliding-window/chunked attention can cap cache growth.

Rule_Description: Online serving characterization should record intended concurrent request level or a range when concurrency is a workload constraint.
Inputs: Target concurrency; request rate if applicable
Condition: Workload is concurrency-driven or concurrency is part of SLA testing
Output_Decision: Evaluate latency/throughput at specified concurrency
Exact_Source_Title: Performance Analyzer — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
Evidence: Perf Analyzer supports concurrency mode and reports throughput and latency at each concurrency level.
Applicability: Serving stack and request pattern specific.
Limitations: Concurrency is not equivalent to batch size; continuous/dynamic batching can change the relationship.

Rule_Description: A latency-sensitive inference workload must define its latency target and metric before resource sizing.
Condition: Latency-sensitive/online workload is specified
Output_Decision: Candidate configuration must be evaluated against specified latency target
Hardware_Field: Latency/Performance field (exact catalogue field not confirmed)
Evidence: MLPerf Inference defines scenario-specific performance requirements; Triton tooling measures latency and percentiles.
Limitations: No universal latency threshold; target percentile and latency definition must be specified.

Rule_Description: An inference workload must define a target throughput metric appropriate to its serving scenario.
Condition: Throughput is a workload requirement
Output_Decision: Use workload-defined throughput target for capacity evaluation
Evidence: MLPerf Inference uses scenario-specific metrics; GenAI-Perf reports request throughput and output token throughput.
Limitations: Do not substitute requests/s for tokens/s without a workload-specific relationship.

Rule_Name: Inference KV Cache Separate From Weight Memory
Rule_Description: For autoregressive transformer inference using KV caching, KV-cache memory must be modeled as a separate component from model weight memory.
Inputs: Model weights; KV cache; context length; batch/concurrency
Condition: Autoregressive model uses KV cache
Output_Decision: Do not represent total inference GPU memory as weight memory alone
Evidence: TensorRT-LLM allocates KV cache separately; Transformers documents dynamic KV-cache growth.
Applicability: Autoregressive transformer serving with KV cache.
Limitations: Exact KV-cache bytes depend on architecture, KV heads, head dimension, layers, dtype, cache layout and parallelism.

Rule_Name: Inference KV Cache Increases With Batch And Context
Rule_Description: For KV-cache-based inference, increasing batch size or context/new-token capacity increases KV-cache demand under the documented runtime model.
Inputs: Batch size; max context length; max new tokens; KV-cache configuration
Condition: KV cache is enabled and runtime uses documented linear sizing behavior
Output_Decision: Increase KV-cache memory allocation or reduce admission limits when workload requires more batch/context capacity
Evidence: TensorRT-LLM documents KV-cache memory as linearly dependent on batch size and max_context_length+max_new_tokens in the Python runtime.
Limitations: Do not generalize the runtime relationship into a universal multiplier for all models/runtimes.

Rule_Name: Inference Runtime Memory Overhead Must Be Accounted
Rule_Description: GPU memory sizing must leave room for runtime/input/output/cache overhead rather than allocating all GPU memory to model weights.
Inputs: GPU total memory; model weights; KV cache; input/output buffers; runtime memory
Condition: Inference deployment uses GPU memory for runtime execution
Threshold_Value: Candidate usable memory after runtime reservations
Output_Decision: Candidate passes only if non-weight memory requirements fit within usable GPU memory
Official_URL: KV cache allocation from remaining free GPU memory
Evidence: TensorRT-LLM sizes KV cache from remaining free GPU memory; HF continuous batching notes input buffers and KV blocks share memory budget.
Limitations: No universal overhead percentage should be assumed.

Rule_Description: When a supported quantization scheme lowers weight precision, the model weight memory footprint is reduced relative to the corresponding higher-precision representation, subject to quantization overhead.
Inputs: Original weight precision; quantized precision; model weights
Condition: Quantization is supported and applied to model weights
Output_Decision: Use quantized weight representation in model-memory accounting
Evidence: Hugging Face states quantization reduces memory footprint; int8 uses fewer bytes than fp32 and int4 halves int8 storage.
Limitations: Do not assume quantized weights reduce KV cache by the same ratio; KV-cache precision is separately configurable in some runtimes.

Rule_Name: Inference Precision Must Be Supported By Candidate GPU
Rule_Description: A candidate GPU should have documented support for the selected inference precision before its precision-specific performance field is used.
Inputs: Selected precision; candidate GPU architecture; catalogue precision performance fields
Condition: Selected precision is used for inference
Output_Decision: Reject or flag candidate if required precision support/performance is unavailable or unverified
Evidence: The catalogue contains precision-specific compute fields, including FP32/FP16/BF16/FP8 where available, with blank/Not stated values for some measurements.
Applicability: Catalogue version and vendor documentation dependent.
Limitations: Field presence is not itself proof of software/kernel support; retain verification status/source.

Rule_Name: Inference Token Throughput Must Be Measured Separately
Rule_Description: LLM inference performance should record output token throughput separately from request throughput when token generation is the resource metric.
Inputs: Output token count; benchmark duration; request count
Condition: LLM/generative inference is evaluated
Output_Decision: Use output-token throughput for token-oriented capacity calculations
Evidence: GenAI-Perf reports output token throughput and request throughput as distinct metrics.
Limitations: Output token throughput does not by itself capture prompt/prefill cost or latency.

Rule_Name: Inference Request Throughput Must Be Measured Separately
Rule_Description: Inference capacity planning should retain request throughput separately from token throughput.
Condition: Request-serving workload is evaluated
Output_Decision: Use request throughput for request-rate capacity calculations
Evidence: GenAI-Perf reports request throughput separately from output token throughput; Triton reports inferences/second.
Limitations: Requests can have different input/output lengths, so requests/s is not interchangeable with tokens/s.

Rule_Name: Throughput-Based GPU Count From Measured Candidate Throughput
Rule_Description: When candidate performance is measured under the same workload configuration, a preliminary throughput-based GPU count can be derived from required throughput divided by validated per-GPU throughput.
Inputs: Required throughput; validated throughput per GPU
Condition: Comparable per-GPU benchmark exists and scaling assumption is explicit
Output_Decision: Preliminary GPU-count lower bound based on throughput; validate latency and memory separately
Exact_Source_Title: Performance Analyzer — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
Evidence: Perf Analyzer measures throughput under specified concurrency/request-rate conditions; the count relationship is a derived engineering calculation.
Applicability: Comparable benchmark/load configuration and approximately independent per-GPU serving units.
Limitations: Not a universal scaling law; model parallelism, contention and batching can change scaling.

Rule_Name: Latency-Constrained GPU Sizing Requires Measured Latency At Target Load
Rule_Description: A candidate GPU count is not sufficient for latency-sensitive inference unless measured latency at the intended workload load satisfies the latency target.
Inputs: Candidate GPU count; request rate/concurrency; latency target; measured latency
Condition: Latency-sensitive workload
Output_Decision: Accept candidate sizing only when measured latency satisfies the workload target under comparable load
Exact_Source_Title: Performance Analyzer — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
Official_URL: Latency threshold / concurrency and request-rate search
Evidence: Perf Analyzer can measure latency at each concurrency/request-rate level and stop when a latency threshold is exceeded.
Limitations: Average latency is not equivalent to p95/p99; use the exact SLA metric.

Rule_Description: Classify inference as online when requests are served interactively or against an explicit latency/request-rate requirement.
Inputs: Serving mode; latency target; request rate
Condition: Interactive/request-serving behavior or latency SLA is specified
Output_Decision: Use online-serving resource requirements including request rate, concurrency and latency where applicable
Hardware_Field: Latency/Performance field (exact catalogue field not confirmed)
Evidence: MLPerf defines server-style scenarios with request/latency requirements; Triton supports request-rate and concurrency load modes.
Limitations: Do not infer business criticality from the word online; classification is about serving behavior.

Rule_Description: Classify inference as batch/throughput-oriented when requests can be processed without an interactive per-request latency SLA and throughput is the primary resource objective.
Inputs: Serving mode; throughput target; latency requirement
Condition: No interactive latency constraint and throughput is primary
Output_Decision: Use throughput-oriented performance characterization
Evidence: MLPerf distinguishes Offline from Server-style inference scenarios; Offline is evaluated with throughput-oriented metrics.
Limitations: Do not treat Offline as identical to every production batch workload.

Rule_Name: LLM Prefill And Decode Metrics Should Be Distinguished
Rule_Description: For generative LLM inference, characterize prompt processing and token generation using available latency/throughput metrics rather than a single generic inference time.
Inputs: Input sequence length; output sequence length; TTFT; inter-token latency; request latency
Condition: Generative LLM serving is evaluated
Output_Decision: Retain TTFT, inter-token latency and request latency when relevant to the SLA
Evidence: GenAI-Perf reports time to first token, inter-token latency, request latency, input/output sequence lengths and output token throughput.
Limitations: These metrics do not directly provide a universal GPU-count formula.

Rule_Name: Inference Benchmark Must Match Serving Configuration
Rule_Description: A candidate inference benchmark result should only be used for resource sizing when model, precision, batch/concurrency, sequence-length and serving configuration are comparable to the target workload.
Inputs: Model; precision; batch; concurrency; sequence lengths; GPU; software/runtime; benchmark scenario
Condition: Benchmark result is used for DSS sizing
Output_Decision: Use benchmark result only within its validated applicability context
Exact_Source_Title: Performance Analyzer — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
Evidence: Triton performance varies with concurrency, batch and load mode; therefore benchmark context must be preserved.
Limitations: This refines the existing benchmark-context rules rather than replacing them.

Rule_Name: No universal fixed multiplier for weights + KV cache + activations + runtime overhead was supported.
Rule_Description: Do not create one; use component accounting plus framework/runtime measurement.

Category: Universal KV-cache memory formula across all architectures
Rule_Name: A single formula cannot safely cover all attention/cache layouts, MQA/GQA, sliding-window/chunked attention, compression and offloading.
Rule_Description: Use IRR-F-02 only as a conventional-cache derived model and require runtime-specific validation.

Category: Universal GPU count from model parameter count
Rule_Name: Parameter count does not determine throughput, latency or memory under all inference runtimes.
Rule_Description: Use measured workload-specific performance and memory feasibility.

Rule_Name: Scaling depends on tensor/model parallelism, interconnect, runtime and workload shape.
Rule_Description: Do not assume linear scaling; require benchmark evidence.

Rule_Name: The reviewed inference sources did not establish a general DSS redundancy multiplier for GPU count.
Rule_Description: Keep redundancy as a separate availability/architecture requirement when supported by the project's availability methodology; do not embed a universal factor here.

Rule_Name: Sources show batching changes throughput/latency, but no universal optimal batch size exists.
Rule_Description: Treat batch size as a workload/runtime tuning variable constrained by SLA and memory.

Rule_Name: Lower precision can reduce memory and may accelerate supported operations, but speedup depends on hardware, kernels and workload.
Rule_Description: Use catalogue precision performance fields and workload-specific benchmarks.

Rule_Name: Weight quantization and KV-cache precision are distinct choices in modern runtimes.
Rule_Description: Model KV-cache dtype explicitly; do not infer KV-cache memory from weight precision alone.
